tools.name: create_machine
tools.description: Boot one of the machines jsbeeb emulates and return a session ID for use with all other tools. The machine runs until the BASIC prompt before this call returns.

model.description: Machine to emulate: B-DFS1.2 (BBC B with 8271 (DFS 1.2)), B-DFS0.9 (BBC B with 8271 (DFS 0.9)), B1770 (BBC B with 1770 (DFS)), B1770A (BBC B with 1770 (ADFS)), B-stock (BBC B (stock)), B-US (BBC B (US)), B-German (BBC B (German)), B-MOS0.10 (BBC B (MOS 0.10)), Master (BBC Master 128 (DFS)), MasterADFS (BBC Master 128 (ADFS)), MasterANFS (BBC Master 128 (ANFS)), Atom (Acorn Atom (MMC)), Atom-Tape (Acorn Atom (Tape)), Atom-Tape-FP (Acorn Atom (Tape with FP)), Atom-DOS (Acorn Atom (DOS))

boot_timeout_secs.description: Max seconds of emulated time to wait for the boot prompt

tube.description: Attach the second processor this model was sold with: a 3MHz 65C02 for a BBC B, or the 4MHz 65C102 Turbo board for a Master

econet.description: Fit Econet, with a file server on the network. A Master gets the ANFS ROM too: *NET, then *I AM SYST logs on (MasterANFS boots into it, so *NET is not needed). A BBC B gets the network hardware but no NFS ROM, so it cannot log on. Not on the Atom

station_id.description: This machine's Econet station number, with econet (default 101)

video_nula.description: Fit a VideoNuLA in place of the video ULA, for programs that use its extended palette and modes (written at &FE22 and &FE23). Not on the Atom

extra_roms.description: Sideways ROMs to fit in the banks the model leaves free, highest first, passing over its sideways RAM. Fails if there are not enough free banks. Not on the Atom

items.description: A sideways ROM image, as jsbeeb names one: a file under jsbeeb's own roms folder by its name there ('ats-3.0.rom', 'b1770/zADFS.ROM'), a file: URL for any other file on this machine (a bare path is looked for under that folder), an http(s): URL, or 'github:owner/repo[@ref]/path'. A zip holding a .rom is opened

bank_roms.description: Sideways ROMs to fit in the banks they name, before extra_roms fill the rest. Fails for a bank the model has no socket for (B-stock and B-MOS0.10 have only 12 to 15), one its own ROMs or fittings fill, or one named twice. A sideways RAM bank takes the image as its contents. Not on the Atom

bank.description: The sideways bank to fit it in

rom.description: A sideways ROM image, as jsbeeb names one: a file under jsbeeb's own roms folder by its name there ('ats-3.0.rom', 'b1770/zADFS.ROM'), a file: URL for any other file on this machine (a bare path is looked for under that folder), an http(s): URL, or 'github:owner/repo[@ref]/path'. A zip holding a .rom is opened

tools.name: destroy_machine
tools.description: Destroy a BBC Micro session and free its resources.

tools.name: load_disc
tools.description: Put a disc image in a drive, from a file on this machine (image_path) or from the archives or a URL (image_ref). Zips are opened and the disc inside used. After loading, use type_input to issue DFS commands (e.g. '*RUN hello', '*DIR', 'CHAIN""'); a disc in drive 1 is reached as ':1.name'.

image_path.description: Absolute path to a disc image on this machine: .ssd, .dsd, .adf, or a zip holding one

image_ref.description: A disc as jsbeeb's own URL names it: 'sth:Acornsoft/Elite.zip' for a Stairway to Hell disc, 'hfe:<path>' for one from the BBC disc archive, 'bitshifters:<path>' for one of the Bitshifters' demos, 'github:owner/repo[@ref]/path' for a file in a GitHub repo (ref '~latest' is the tag of its latest release), or an http(s) or file: URL

drive.description: Drive to put the disc in

tools.name: load_tape
tools.description: Put a tape (.uef, or a zip holding one) in the cassette recorder and press PLAY. The Atom's tape runs at once; on a BBC or Master it runs when the OS starts the motor, so follow with type_input '*TAPE' and then 'CHAIN""' (or '*RUN', 'LOAD""').

image_path.description: Absolute path to a tape image on this machine

image_ref.description: A tape by URL: http(s), file:, or 'github:owner/repo[@ref]/path' as for discs

tools.name: load_basic
tools.description: Tokenise BBC BASIC source code and load it into the emulator's PAGE memory, exactly as if you had typed it in and saved it. Does NOT run the program.

source.description: BBC BASIC source code (plain text, BBC dialect)

tools.name: type_input
tools.description: Type text at the current keyboard prompt (simulates key presses). RETURN is pressed once after the text, unless the text already ends in a newline. Use run_until_prompt after this to collect output. A breakpoint stops the typing part way: completed is false, the breakpoint and registers are reported, and the rest is typed as the machine runs on; until then key_down and key_up refuse, and release_all_keys drops it.

tools.name: run_until_prompt
tools.description: Run the emulator until it returns to a keyboard input prompt (e.g. the BASIC prompt after RUN completes). Returns all text output that was written to the screen since the last call.

timeout_secs.description: Max emulated seconds to run before giving up

clear.description: If true (default), clear the output buffer after returning it. Pass false to peek at accumulated output without consuming it.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture the last fully-painted BBC Micro frame as a PNG image. Returns a base64-encoded PNG of the full 1024×625 emulated display, plus the frame counter so you can tell a genuinely new frame from the same one captured twice. Tip: call run_until_prompt first to let the screen settle, or run_frames to step to the next frame.

active_only.description: If true, crop to the active display area and apply 2× pixel scaling for clarity

tools.name: read_memory
tools.description: Read bytes from the BBC Micro's memory map. Returns an array of decimal byte values plus a hex dump, and paging: romsel as last written, bank (the sideways bank it pages in at &8000–&BFFF) and on a Master acccon, so a read of paged memory says which bank it came from. Pass bank or shadow to read a particular one instead.

bank.description: Sideways ROM/RAM bank to page at &8000–&BFFF for this access, instead of the one ROMSEL selects (12 to 15 on B-stock and B-MOS0.10, which have four sockets)

shadow.description: On a Master, use shadow RAM (true) or main RAM (false) at &3000–&7FFF, whatever ACCCON says

tools.name: write_memory
tools.description: Write bytes into the BBC Micro's memory. Useful for poking machine code, modifying variables, or patching running programs. Pass bank or shadow to write into a particular bank, as for read_memory.

bytes.description: Array of byte values to write

bank.description: Sideways ROM/RAM bank to page at &8000–&BFFF for this access, instead of the one ROMSEL selects (12 to 15 on B-stock and B-MOS0.10, which have four sockets)

shadow.description: On a Master, use shadow RAM (true) or main RAM (false) at &3000–&7FFF, whatever ACCCON says

tools.name: read_registers
tools.description: Read the current 6502 CPU register state (PC, A, X, Y, stack pointer, processor status), along with the frame and cycle counters.

tools.name: run_for_cycles
tools.description: Run the emulator for a number of CPU cycles (2MHz on a BBC, 1MHz on an Atom): that many to within the instruction that finishes it, unless a breakpoint stops it first. Useful for precise timing, or just to advance the clock a bit between interactions. Do not use this to step frames: a frame is 40000 cycles with interlace on (the default) but 39936 with it off, so a fixed step drifts against the display. Use run_frames instead. Reports cycles_run, the cycles actually executed, and accumulated text output. A breakpoint stops the run early: completed is false, stopped_reason is 'breakpoint', and the registers (with elapsed_cycles) show where it stopped; the next call runs on from there. A breakpoint hit during an earlier call that did not report it is reported first, with stopped_reason 'pending_breakpoint' and cycles_run 0. By default the output buffer is cleared after returning — pass clear=false when using this as an intermediate step (e.g. between key_down and key_up) to avoid losing output that you want to collect later via run_until_prompt.

cycles.description: Number of CPU cycles to execute

clear.description: If true (default), clear the output buffer after returning it. Pass false to peek.

tools.name: run_frames
tools.description: Run the emulator until it has painted another `count` frames, stopping on the paint itself. Use this rather than run_for_cycles for anything frame-oriented: capturing consecutive screenshots to see flicker or tearing, or stepping an animation. One frame is exactly one new screenshot. Reports frames_run, cycles_run, and frame_count (which only ever climbs, so compare it across calls to confirm the screen really did move on). completed is false if the machine stopped painting or a breakpoint fired first; a breakpoint stop reports stopped_reason 'breakpoint' and the registers, or 'pending_breakpoint' for a hit an earlier call left unreported, as run_for_cycles does.

clear.description: If true (default), clear the output buffer after returning it. Pass false to peek.

tools.name: run_until_address
tools.description: Run until the PC reaches an address, stopping before the instruction there runs, or until timeout_secs of emulated time pass. Like a one-off execute breakpoint: give bank to stop only while that sideways bank is paged in. reached says whether it got there; stopped_reason is 'address', 'timeout', or 'breakpoint' if a set breakpoint fired first ('pending_breakpoint', with cycles_run 0 and reached false as nothing ran, for a hit an earlier call left unreported, as run_for_cycles does). An execute breakpoint on the address itself still reports reached true and 'address', with that breakpoint attached. Every result reports address, bank if given, cycles_run, the registers where it stopped, and the text output. The next run starts with the instruction it stopped at.

bank.description: Only stop while this sideways bank is paged in at &8000–&BFFF, to stop in one ROM (12 to 15 on B-stock and B-MOS0.10)

timeout_secs.description: Max emulated seconds to run before giving up

clear.description: If true (default), clear the output buffer after returning it. Pass false to peek.

tools.name: key_down
tools.description: Press and hold a key on the keyboard; use key_up to release it later. Name the key one way: by the machine's own name for it, or by BBC internal key number, INKEY number, or col and row, which is how to press exactly the key a game's own keyboard scan reads. Every way presses the matrix key itself, so what goes down is what keyboard_state reports. Reports the key that went down, with name and numbers.

key.description: The key as the machine's own keyboard names it, which is how keyboard_state reports it. On a BBC or Master: SHIFT, CTRL, RETURN, SPACE, DELETE, ESCAPE, TAB, CAPSLOCK, SHIFTLOCK, COPY, UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT, F0–F9, A–Z, K0–K9 for the digits, and the engraved punctuation keys such as COMMA, SEMICOLON_PLUS, COLON_STAR, AT, HAT_TILDE. The Atom has its own set: SHIFT, CTRL, RETURN, REPT, LOCK, COPY, DELETE, ESCAPE, arrows, A–Z, K0–K9, MINUS_EQUALS and the like. An unknown name is refused with the full list for the model

internal.description: BBC internal key number, as OSBYTE 121 and a game's keyboard scan use (X is 66, SPACE is 98)

inkey.description: Negative INKEY number, -1 to -128 (X is -67, SPACE is -99); the internal number is -inkey - 1

col.description: Keyboard matrix column, given with row

row.description: Keyboard matrix row, given with col

tools.name: key_up
tools.description: Release a held key, named any of the ways key_down takes. Reports the matrix keys that came up.

key.description: The key as the machine's own keyboard names it, which is how keyboard_state reports it. On a BBC or Master: SHIFT, CTRL, RETURN, SPACE, DELETE, ESCAPE, TAB, CAPSLOCK, SHIFTLOCK, COPY, UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT, F0–F9, A–Z, K0–K9 for the digits, and the engraved punctuation keys such as COMMA, SEMICOLON_PLUS, COLON_STAR, AT, HAT_TILDE. The Atom has its own set: SHIFT, CTRL, RETURN, REPT, LOCK, COPY, DELETE, ESCAPE, arrows, A–Z, K0–K9, MINUS_EQUALS and the like. An unknown name is refused with the full list for the model

internal.description: BBC internal key number, as OSBYTE 121 and a game's keyboard scan use (X is 66, SPACE is 98)

inkey.description: Negative INKEY number, -1 to -128 (X is -67, SPACE is -99); the internal number is -inkey - 1

col.description: Keyboard matrix column, given with row

row.description: Keyboard matrix row, given with col

tools.name: keyboard_state
tools.description: Report the keyboard as the machine sees it: every key held, with its matrix column and row, its name, and on a BBC its internal key number (as OSBYTE 121 and a keyboard scan use) and negative INKEY number; and whether typing from an interrupted type_input is still pending. Check this before a test that assumes nothing is held.

tools.name: release_all_keys
tools.description: Release every held key and drop any typing still pending from an interrupted type_input, so the keyboard is in a known state. Reports what was released.

tools.name: flush_keyboard_buffer
tools.description: Empty the OS's keyboard buffer, throwing away keys pressed but not yet read, so a program that is busy when they go down does not read them later. Unlike OSBYTE 21 it leaves a function key's expansion still to come. Not on the Atom, whose OS has no buffer.

tools.name: reset
tools.description: Reset the BBC Micro. With autoboot=true, holds SHIFT during reset to trigger a disc autoboot (SHIFT+BREAK) and reports shift_held_at_reset. The boot sequence is initiated but not run to completion — use run_for_cycles or run_until_prompt afterwards as needed. Typing left pending by an interrupted type_input is dropped first (cancelled_typing).

hard.description: Hard reset (power-on) if true, soft reset if false

autoboot.description: Hold SHIFT during reset to autoboot the disc in drive 0

tools.name: boot_disc
tools.description: Load a disc image, from a file here or from the archives or a URL as load_disc takes them, and autoboot it (SHIFT+BREAK). Equivalent to: load_disc → key_down SHIFT → reset → key_up SHIFT. The boot sequence is initiated but not run to completion — use run_for_cycles or run_until_prompt afterwards as needed. Reports shift_held_at_reset, and cancelled_typing if an interrupted type_input had to be dropped first.

image_path.description: Absolute path to a disc image on this machine: .ssd, .dsd, .adf, or a zip holding one

image_ref.description: A disc as jsbeeb's own URL names it: 'sth:Acornsoft/Elite.zip' for a Stairway to Hell disc, 'hfe:<path>' for one from the BBC disc archive, 'bitshifters:<path>' for one of the Bitshifters' demos, 'github:owner/repo[@ref]/path' for a file in a GitHub repo (ref '~latest' is the tag of its latest release), or an http(s) or file: URL

tools.name: run_disc
tools.description: One-shot convenience tool: boot a BBC Micro, load a disc image, autoboot it (SHIFT+BREAK), return all text output and optionally a screenshot, then destroy the session. Like run_basic but for disc images.

source.description: BBC BASIC source code to run

timeout_secs.description: Max emulated seconds to allow the program to run

screenshot.description: Include a screenshot of the final screen state

tools.name: read_sound_state
tools.description: Read the SN76489 sound chip's current register state: tone periods for channels 0–2, noise register, volume/attenuation for all 4 channels, LFSR state, and which register is latched. Useful for verifying what the program has written to the sound chip.

tools.name: start_sound_capture
tools.description: Start capturing all SN76489 sound chip writes. Every byte written to the chip is logged with its cycle timestamp. Use stop_sound_capture to retrieve the log. Clears any previous capture.

tools.name: stop_sound_capture
tools.description: Stop capturing SN76489 writes and return the log. Each entry has a cycle timestamp and the byte value written. The values are decoded into human-readable form (channel, tone/volume, value).

max_entries.description: Maximum number of entries to return (most recent if exceeded)

tools.name: set_breakpoint
tools.description: Set a persistent breakpoint. The breakpoint stays active across multiple run_for_cycles calls until removed with clear_breakpoint. When a breakpoint fires, run_for_cycles returns early and reports which breakpoint was hit. Types: 'execute' (PC reaches address), 'read' (memory read), 'write' (memory write). An address in &8000–&BFFF is in whichever sideways ROM is paged in; give bank to stop in one ROM only.

type.description: Breakpoint type: execute (PC), read (memory read), write (memory write)

bank.description: Only break while this sideways bank is paged in at &8000–&BFFF, to stop in one ROM (12 to 15 on B-stock and B-MOS0.10)

tools.name: clear_breakpoint
tools.description: Remove a previously set breakpoint by its ID, or pass id=0 to clear all breakpoints.

id.description: Breakpoint ID to remove (0 = clear all)

tools.name: step_back
tools.description: Step the machine back one instruction, or with over back over the call the last instruction returned from, or with to_cycle back to that cycle (an instruction's start, as who_wrote reports one). Replays the history the session keeps (see the history tool) from a snapshot before where it lands. It replays text from type_input, but cannot go back past something no replay can repeat: a load_basic, a disc or tape change, a write to a disc, a write_memory with bank or shadow, a read_memory of a device register, or the cassette motor running, and an Econet machine keeps no history; reset (hard) and restore_state start the history afresh. While type_input is still typing (a breakpoint stopped it part way) it refuses: run on to finish the text (after a restore_state, running on drops it instead), or release_all_keys to drop it. When it cannot go back, moved is false, refusal says why, and the machine is left as it was. A step back leaves breakpoint hits cleared and the captured text as it was, counts no frames, and captures no sound writes. Reports moved, and where it landed as read_registers does.

over.description: Step back over the call the last instruction returned from

to_cycle.description: Step back to this elapsed cycle instead, as who_wrote gives a write's cycle

tools.name: step_back_out
tools.description: Step the machine back to the JSR, BRK or interrupt that entered the routine it is in, the reverse of running to its RTS or RTI. Replays the history the session keeps (see the history tool) from a snapshot before where it lands. It replays text from type_input, but cannot go back past something no replay can repeat: a load_basic, a disc or tape change, a write to a disc, a write_memory with bank or shadow, a read_memory of a device register, or the cassette motor running, and an Econet machine keeps no history; reset (hard) and restore_state start the history afresh. While type_input is still typing (a breakpoint stopped it part way) it refuses: run on to finish the text (after a restore_state, running on drops it instead), or release_all_keys to drop it. When it cannot go back, moved is false, refusal says why, and the machine is left as it was. A step back leaves breakpoint hits cleared and the captured text as it was, counts no frames, and captures no sound writes.

tools.name: reverse_continue
tools.description: Run the machine backwards to where it would have stopped at the newest hit of any breakpoint set with set_breakpoint before now: before the instruction for an execute breakpoint, after the instruction for a read or write. Running on from there does not stop at the same breakpoint again. Replays the history the session keeps (see the history tool) from a snapshot before where it lands. It replays text from type_input, but cannot go back past something no replay can repeat: a load_basic, a disc or tape change, a write to a disc, a write_memory with bank or shadow, a read_memory of a device register, or the cassette motor running, and an Econet machine keeps no history; reset (hard) and restore_state start the history afresh. While type_input is still typing (a breakpoint stopped it part way) it refuses: run on to finish the text (after a restore_state, running on drops it instead), or release_all_keys to drop it. When it cannot go back, moved is false, refusal says why, and the machine is left as it was. A step back leaves breakpoint hits cleared and the captured text as it was, counts no frames, and captures no sound writes.

tools.name: who_wrote
tools.description: Find the last write to a byte, as the machine pages it now, by replaying the history the session keeps, newest first, and leaving the machine as it was. found says whether a write was found. A write reports pc and pcHex, the instruction that wrote it (null when an input such as write_memory did), value, the cycle it started at (step_back with to_cycle goes there), and cycles_ago and seconds_ago. With nothing found, searched_cycles and why say how far back it looked and why it went no further; refusal says why it could not search at all (no history, ROM, or something it cannot replay since the newest snapshot).

tools.name: history
tools.description: See, or set, how much history the session keeps for step_back, step_back_out, reverse_continue and who_wrote. Each machine starts keeping what the jsbeeb page keeps: 3 recent snapshots, at most one a frame, and 30 more, at most one a second, each about 130KB on a Master to 200KB on a B (65KB more with a tube); keeping them slows a run somewhat. An Econet machine keeps none, and refuses to start. Give recent or seconds to change it (both 0 turns history off; a lone ring of 1 holds only the newest snapshot, which leaves a step back nothing to start from), which forgets the history kept so far. Reports the sizes, how many snapshots there are, and how far back the oldest reaches.

recent.description: Recent snapshots to keep, at most one a frame

seconds.description: Snapshots to keep further back, at most one a second

tools.name: start_coverage
tools.description: Start recording which instructions the host CPU executes, and how often, as the machine runs under any tool. Addresses in &8000–&BFFF are kept apart by the sideways bank paged in (and on a Master, ANDY over &8000–&8FFF); HAZEL and shadow RAM count as the plain address. Recording never stops the machine, and carries on across reset, boot_disc and restore_state. An instruction the machine is stopped at has already been counted, even if stop_coverage comes before it runs. Use stop_coverage to stop and get the summary. Starting again discards what was recorded so far.

tools.name: stop_coverage
tools.description: Stop recording coverage and summarise it: instructions_executed, unique_addresses, the stretches of code executed (ranges, each from the first to the last instruction address run in it, with bank (0–15, or 'andy') for &8000–&BFFF, the count of addresses and executions in it), and hot_spots, the addresses run most often. Over max_ranges stretches, the busiest are kept; ranges_total says how many there were.

max_ranges.description: Most stretches of code to list

max_hot_spots.description: Most hot spot addresses to list

tools.name: save_state
tools.description: Snapshot the whole machine (CPU, RAM, sideways RAM, video, sound chip, discs, tube) and keep it server-side under a state ID. Econet's file server is not in it, so a machine restored from it may need to log on again. Booting is the slow part of a session, so snapshotting once and restoring between attempts is much cheaper than creating a machine for each one. The snapshot itself never crosses this connection, only its ID.

label.description: Optional note to identify this state in list_states

tools.name: restore_state
tools.description: Put a session back to a state saved by save_state. Memory, registers and the cycle count rewind; breakpoints and the frame counter carry on. A state saved where an execute breakpoint or run_until_address stopped the machine runs on past that instruction when next run; otherwise an execute breakpoint at the restored PC fires (read and write breakpoints stop after their instruction has run). The target session need not be the one the state was saved from, so a state can be restored into several machines to run from the same start point, but it must be the same model with the same tube, Econet, station number and VideoNuLA. Sideways ROMs come with the state, replacing the target's own.

tools.name: list_states
tools.description: List the states held by save_state, newest first.

session_id.description: Only list states saved from this session (default: all)

tools.name: delete_state
tools.description: Discard a saved state and free the memory it holds. States outlive the session they came from, so they are only freed when deleted.

tools.name: save_memory
tools.description: Save a range of the BBC Micro's memory to a file on the host filesystem. Much faster than multiple read_memory calls for large dumps. Reports paging as read_memory does, and takes bank or shadow the same way.

path.description: Absolute path to write the file to

bank.description: Sideways ROM/RAM bank to page at &8000–&BFFF for this access, instead of the one ROMSEL selects (12 to 15 on B-stock and B-MOS0.10, which have four sockets)

shadow.description: On a Master, use shadow RAM (true) or main RAM (false) at &3000–&7FFF, whatever ACCCON says

tools.name: disassemble
tools.description: Disassemble 6502 machine code from the BBC Micro's memory. Returns assembly listing with addresses, hex bytes, and mnemonics.
